identity.title: Scrubber Pressure-Drop Log and C-1 Carbon Outlet Detector-Tube Check — August and September 2026

scan.summary: This is a log of equipment performance monitoring maintained by Cascade Specialty Chemicals at their Portland facility to satisfy conditions of their Standard Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01. The log records daily pressure-drop measurements across two scrubbers (S-1 for acid repackaging, S-2 for caustic repackaging) to ensure they remain between 2.0 and 6.0 inches of water column, and weekly breakthrough checks on a carbon unit outlet. The document shows recorded readings from August 1–31 and September 1–25, 2026, with one excursion on September 9 requiring attention.
scan.freshness_note: This record was last updated on September 25, 2026 for the daily log and September 21, 2026 for the weekly detector-tube check. The document is current but incomplete: supervisor review signatures and dates are blank, which is required for closure of the record.

gaps.title: Missing supervisor review signature and date
gaps.description: The log contains a line for supervisor review signature and date at the bottom of each month's section, but these fields are blank for both August and September. The permit condition requires record-keeping; supervisory sign-off is standard practice for monitoring records to confirm their accuracy and completeness before filing.
gaps.fix: Have a supervisor review and sign the record with the date, confirming that all required readings have been taken and are within or outside acceptable limits.
gaps.citation: Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01, Condition 3.1 (pressure drop monitoring) and Condition 3.3 (detector-tube checks)
gaps.locator: Bottom of August section and bottom of September section (both pages)

gaps.title: S-2 pressure drop exceeded upper limit on September 9
gaps.description: On September 9, 2026, the S-2 (caustic repackaging line) scrubber recorded a pressure drop of 6.4 inches of water column. The permit condition 3.1 requires that pressure drop be kept between 2.0 and 6.0 inches whenever the line is operating. A reading of 6.4 exceeds the 6.0 upper limit.
gaps.fix: Document the cause of the excursion (nozzle clogging, scaling, equipment malfunction, or other), the corrective action taken, and when normal operation was restored. This should be recorded in the Notes column or in a separate incident log. Verify that S-2 was brought back into compliance on the next operating day (September 10 shows 4.6, which is compliant).
gaps.locator: September 9, 2026 row; S-2 ΔP column; Notes field shows no explanation

gaps.title: Missing detector-tube check for week of August 14 and two weeks in September
gaps.description: The permit condition 3.3 requires a weekly check for breakthrough at the C-1 carbon unit outlet. The August detector-tube log shows checks for weeks starting Aug 3, 10, 17, 24, and 31 (5 checks). However, there is a gap: no entry is shown for the week of August 14, even though the scrubber log shows the caustic line ran on August 14. In September, only two checks are recorded (weeks of Sep 7 and Sep 21), but the September scrubber log shows operation through September 25. The weeks of Sep 14 and Sep 28 are missing.
gaps.fix: Complete missing detector-tube checks. For the week of August 14, retroactively verify whether a check was conducted and record it, or document why it was skipped (e.g., planned downtime). For September weeks 14 and 28, conduct the checks now if the carbon unit is still in service, record the date and result, and implement a system to ensure weekly checks are not missed going forward.
gaps.locator: August weekly check table (5 entries for 5 expected weeks) and September weekly check table (2 entries, but through Sept 25 indicates at least 4 weeks)
gaps.quote: Condition 3.3: weekly check for breakthrough at the C-1 carbon unit outlet

conditions.title: Record pressure drop across each scrubber once per operating day
conditions.evidence_expected: Daily magnehelic gauge readings for S-1 and S-2, recorded in a log with date, line operation status (Y/N), pressure drop in inches of water column, operator name, and any notes. Readings must be maintained between 2.0 and 6.0 inches of water column when the line is operating.

conditions.title: Keep pressure drop within 2.0–6.0 inches of water column during operation
conditions.evidence_expected: All recorded pressure drops within the specified range, or documentation of when an out-of-range reading occurred, the cause, and the corrective action taken and date brought back into compliance.

conditions.title: Conduct weekly checks for breakthrough at the C-1 carbon unit outlet
conditions.evidence_expected: Weekly detector-tube readings at the carbon outlet, recorded with the week start date, ppm reading, whether breakthrough was detected (Yes/No), and the name of the person who conducted the check. A baseline reading of 0 ppm indicates proper function.

deadlines.title: Conduct weekly C-1 outlet detector-tube check
deadlines.source_line: Condition 3.3: 'weekly check for breakthrough at the C-1 carbon unit outlet'

facts.value: S-2 (caustic repackaging line) scrubber pressure drops range from 4.0 to 4.4 inches of water column in August and 4.1 to 6.4 inches in September, with one excursion to 6.4 on Sep 9
facts.quote: S-2 ΔP readings: August range 4.0–4.4, September range 4.1–6.4 (excursion on Sep 9)
facts.locator: August scrubber log and September scrubber log, S-2 ΔP columns
facts.affects: S-2 operates higher in the pressure-drop range than S-1, and the excursion on September 9 indicates a possible partial blockage, scaling, or equipment issue requiring investigation and correction.

facts.value: S-2 pressure drop exceeded permit limit (6.4 in. w.c. vs. 6.0 max) on September 9, 2026
facts.locator: September scrubber log, Sept 9 row, S-2 ΔP column
facts.affects: Indicates potential scrubber clogging or fouling on the caustic line and requires root-cause investigation and documentation of corrective action to ensure permit compliance.

facts.value: C-1 carbon unit shows 0 ppm breakthrough detection in all 7 recorded weeks (August and September 2026), indicating the carbon is still functioning and has not been reached saturation or breakthrough
facts.quote: Tube reading (ppm): all entries 0; Breakthrough?: all 'No'
facts.locator: August weekly check table and September weekly check table
facts.affects: The carbon unit is performing its intended function. No immediate replacement is required, but the company should continue monitoring and be prepared to replace the carbon if breakthrough (ppm > 0) is detected.

facts.value: Two scrubbers in operation: S-1 (acid repackaging line) and S-2 (caustic repackaging line); one carbon unit C-1 at outlet

expected_missing.title: Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01 itself
expected_missing.why: The record references and must be read in conjunction with the permit document to confirm the exact limits, monitoring frequency, and reporting requirements
expected_missing.basis: similar companies maintain their actual permits alongside monitoring logs for verification

expected_missing.title: Monthly or quarterly summary report to Oregon DEQ
expected_missing.why: Standard air permits often require facilities to submit monthly or quarterly summaries of monitoring data to the agency, or to report excursions within a certain timeframe (e.g., 24 hours)
expected_missing.basis: similar companies must report permit excursions to DEQ; this log alone does not show evidence of DEQ notification of the Sep 9 excursion

expected_missing.title: Root-cause analysis and corrective-action report for the September 9 S-2 excursion
expected_missing.why: When a permit condition limit is exceeded, permit holders are typically required to determine why, what was done to correct it, and how recurrence will be prevented
expected_missing.basis: standard permit practice requires documentation of investigation and remedy for out-of-compliance events

expected_missing.title: Maintenance records for scrubbers S-1 and S-2
expected_missing.why: The log notes 'nozzles rinsed' on Aug 14 for S-2, suggesting maintenance is performed; full maintenance logs (frequency, scope, findings) would be expected
expected_missing.basis: scrubber performance depends on maintenance; companies typically keep separate maintenance schedules and records

expected_missing.title: Equipment calibration certificate for magnehelic gauges
expected_missing.why: The log states readings are taken 'at the magnehelic gauge on the scrubber inlet'; these gauges must be calibrated to ensure accuracy
expected_missing.basis: regulatory monitoring requires calibrated instrumentation; facilities maintain calibration records separately from logs

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence in what the log says: all data are clearly readable, dates and readings are explicit, and the permit conditions are stated directly in the document header. The major findings are solid: (1) one excursion on Sep 9 (S-2 at 6.4 in. w.c., exceeding 6.0 max); (2) supervisor review signatures are missing; (3) the weekly detector-tube checks are incomplete (missing week of Aug 14, and weeks of Sep 14 and 28 given operation through Sep 25). The only uncertainty is whether the missing detector-tube entries represent actual skipped checks or data-entry delays. The document does not explain the cause of the Sep 9 excursion or state whether it was reported to DEQ. The company should have the actual permit on file to confirm the exact reporting and retention requirements.
